analysis.title: DeskTalk - FOMC minutes: Few surprises, few doves
key_insights: October FOMC minutes showed few surprises. A "couple" of participants believed an increase of more than 25bp in December could be warranted if incoming inflation data proved unfavorable.

Fed Governor Waller said before the hotter than expected October CPI print (Nov 10) that he favors a 50bp hike in December, and repeated that view today. NY Fed President Williams pushed back, saying the current situation does not warrant such a move. Cleveland Fed's Hammack prefers tightening in "smaller increments".

Markets read the minutes as modestly hawkish. Front-end UST yields rose roughly 2bps, DXY rose to 103.84, and SPX pared minor gains to trade -0.2%. OIS pricing for a January hike rose from 70% to 73%.

Citi US economists expect the Fed to stay highly responsive to inflation data. No further CPI release comes before the December 9 FOMC decision, so Fed commentary will stay under scrutiny until the blackout starts Nov 28.
A sustained equity selloff could eventually reduce the Committee's willingness to extend the hiking cycle beyond December. Citi economists are tracking Core PCE at +0.27%, due Nov 25.
